Inner Network Host Terms

Effective Date: November 10, 2026 · Last updated: November 10, 2026 · Version 2026-11-10

These Host Terms apply when you host an event in Inner Network, invite guests, send texts, or sell tickets. They add to our Terms of Service, and you accept them before your first event with ticket sales or texts. Wavecode, LLC ("we") operates Inner Network.

1. You are the organizer

When you create an event in Inner Network, you or your organization is the host and organizer. We provide tools to publish the event, invite guests, collect RSVPs, check guests in, and sell tickets. We do not organize, run, or supervise your event. You are responsible for the event, its accuracy, permits, venue, safety, accessibility information, and following the law. For wellness events, you are responsible for any waivers, health screening, or qualifications the activity requires. Inner Network is for business and wellness events; we may remove nightlife, dating, or party events.

2. Co-hosts and teams

You can ask other members to co-host. A co-host gets full access only after accepting your request. Organization admins decide whether each member can view or edit the organization's events. Everyone with access can see the guest list, answers, check-ins, sales, and change history, and you are responsible for the people you give access to. We keep a history of who changed what and when.

3. Guest lists

If you add guests by typing, pasting, or uploading a file, you confirm that you got their details lawfully, that they would reasonably expect to hear from you about the event, and that you will use the list only for your events. Do not upload purchased, rented, or scraped lists. Each guest needs a first name, a last name, and an email address or phone number.

4. Emails and texts

Event emails are sent by Inner Network on your behalf and include your name, our mailing address, and an unsubscribe link. An invitation text goes only to an invited guest who does not have an Inner Network profile, and only after you confirm that the guest agreed to hear from you. Reminder texts go only to guests who asked for them. Every text identifies you and says how to opt out, and a reply of STOP stops all Inner Network texts to that number for every host. You must not text anyone who has opted out, and you are responsible for following the Telephone Consumer Protection Act and similar laws. Do not use event emails or texts for unrelated advertising. We may limit or turn off sending for any host.

5. Ticket sales and the platform fee

You sell tickets through Inner Network using Stripe, and you are the seller. To sell, you set up a Stripe connected account and accept Stripe's Connected Account Agreement. From each ticket sale, Inner Network keeps a platform fee of 2% of the ticket price plus Stripe's card processing fee, and the rest goes to your Stripe account. You pay these fees; they are not added to the buyer's price. We will tell you in advance if the platform fee changes, and a change applies only to sales after it takes effect.

6. Refunds and cancellations

You set your event's refund policy and must show it before purchase. If you cancel an event, you must refund every buyer in full. Refunds go back to the original payment method. When a ticket is refunded, the platform fee and Stripe's processing fee are not returned. If you cancel and do not refund buyers, we may issue refunds from your Stripe balance, recover amounts from you, and suspend your ability to sell tickets.

7. Payouts, chargebacks, and taxes

Stripe verifies your identity and sends payouts on its own schedule. We do not hold your funds and are not responsible for Stripe's decisions to delay, hold, or refuse payouts. If a buyer disputes a charge with their bank, you are responsible for the disputed amount and dispute fees, and we or Stripe may recover them from your Stripe balance or future payouts. Answer our requests for proof of the event and of your refund policy promptly. You are responsible for taxes on your ticket income and for any sales or admission tax on your tickets.

8. Listed organizers

If you claim an organizer listing that Inner Network created from public information, you may edit or remove it. Listing your public events is free, and members are sent to your own registration page. If you choose to sell tickets through Inner Network, these Host Terms apply.

9. Ending

We may suspend hosting, ticket sales, or texts for any host who breaks these Host Terms or our Terms of Service. Questions: contact@innernetwork.app.
